### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via registerObject (symbol, a method of class SchemaRegistry))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cdd4eea93811522cca145a0f24858def51443671` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `88053174692167dcb376d8c32d33754139d87f79` — the merge of head `cf6bf094b94601e90a9912f0c0b426e1352f6600` into base `cdd4eea93811522cca145a0f24858def51443671`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 88053174692167dcb376d8c32d33754139d87f79 && git checkout 88053174692167dcb376d8c32d33754139d87f79
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cdd4eea93811522cca145a0f24858def51443671 cf6bf094b94601e90a9912f0c0b426e1352f6600 && git checkout -B drift-repro cdd4eea93811522cca145a0f24858def51443671 && git merge --no-ff cf6bf094b94601e90a9912f0c0b426e1352f6600

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cdd4eea93811522cca145a0f24858def51443671
```

</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cdd4eea93811522cca145a0f24858def51443671` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cf6bf094b94601e90a9912f0c0b426e1352f6600`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/object-own-action-schema-parse.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-package-object-discovery.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/stored-metadata-reader-contexts.pin.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`parsePackageAction`, `registerItem`'s #25649 parse guard, `registerObject` through its `applyProtection` call), packages/metadata-core/src/code-artifact-provenance.ts (`isCodeArtifactBody`, `isTenantAuthored`), packages/spec/src/shared/protection.zod.ts (`applyProtection`), packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts (`ActionSchema`: the script body-or-target refine, the `ai.description` min-40 rule, the `lowerRequiresFeature` / `lowerRequiresMembershipReach` transform), packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts (`ObjectSchema.actions`, `ServiceObject`), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`registerApp`, `stampObjectPackage`, nested-plugin object door, `executeAction`), packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts (residual-object door, metadata-service reload doors, `objectContributionKind`), packages/objectql/src/metadata-facade.ts (`registerObjectBothPlaces`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (the save door write-through and the boot rehydration `registerObject` calls), packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (`isHeadlessInvokableAction`), packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-contract.ts (`FLS_CONTRACT_OBJECT`) and its five in-repo readers, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (ruling A), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (prescription detectors). Prose face read for ②: .changeset/25744-object-own-action-schema-parse.md.

### ① Derived judgments

Read-only: the card body and its three comments (triage 6393644756, claim 6409400948, os-dev-report 6410946806), the PR body, the five-file diff `origin/main...cf6bf094b9` (merge base `9ca36b163e`), and the head's check-runs. Nothing built or run.

**CI on the head, at review time.** 50 check-runs; 42 concluded, 0 non-green; 8 still in progress (`Test Core` shards 1 to 7 of 8, `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace`). Concluded `success` and bearing on this review: `Check Changeset`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` (the ADR-0087 registration gate's family), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path`, `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Test Core (8/8)`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Lint · ESLint`. The judgments below are rendered on what has concluded; the pending shards are the derived test families the dev reports green locally (objectql 470 files / 8738 tests, runtime 446 / 7131, rest, metadata-protocol), and a red there would stand on its own as a gate verdict.

**1. The accept-set change, named.** `SchemaRegistry.registerObject(schema, packageId, …)` now, when `packageId` is truthy AND `isCodeArtifactBody({ _packageId: schema._packageId ?? packageId, _provenance: schema._provenance ?? 'package' })` holds, maps `ActionSchema.safeParse` over `schema.actions` (array, non-empty) and either stores the parsed array on a shallow copy or throws the first failure as `INVALID_METADATA` / `status: 422` / `httpStatus: 422` with `issues[]` paths prefixed `actions.N.` and a message naming action, object and package (registry.ts 205 to 236, 257 to 266, 3503 to 3508 at the head). **Right.** The guard is the exact test `registerItem` applies at its #25649 seam (`type === 'action' && packageId && isCodeArtifactBody(item)`, registry.ts 5302), transposed to run BEFORE `applyProtection`: `applyProtection` (protection.zod.ts 238 to 255) stamps `_packageId` only when undefined and `_provenance = 'package'` only when undefined and a package id is in hand, so the two `??` fallbacks reproduce byte for byte what `isCodeArtifactBody` would read after the stamp at registry.ts 3689. One parse path for both doors, as the card wanted.

**2. Which registrations are now parsed, and what refuses them.** Judged (parsed, or refused 422 `INVALID_METADATA`): `ObjectQL.registerApp` for a raw manifest, array and map branches (engine.ts 9303 / 9316, `packageId = manifest.id`; a manifest with no `version` is still judged because the guard falls back to the `packageId` argument, and `stampObjectPackage` is identity without a version); a `strict: false` `defineStack` handed to `registerApp`; the nested-plugin object door (engine.ts 9479 / 9489, owner = parent id); `AppPlugin`'s residual-object door (plugin.ts 2840); the public `ObjectQL.registerObject(schema, packageId)` proxy; `MetadataFacade.registerObjectBothPlaces` when a real `_packageId` arrives (metadata-facade.ts 191 to 199); the plugin's two metadata-service reload doors (plugin.ts 1361 / 1439, `_packageId ?? 'metadata-service'`, body not tenant-stamped). **Right**, and one reader note the PR body does not carry: at the nested-plugin door and the two reload doors the throw lands in a pre-existing `try/catch` that logs `warn` and skips the object (engine.ts 9492, plugin.ts 1369), so "refused loudly" is a warning line there. That is how every registry refusal on those doors already behaves (the field-`type` door, ownership conflicts), so it is parity, not a fault of this diff.

**3. Untouched as claimed.** A bare `registerObject(schema)` with no `packageId`: the guard's first conjunct fails; `applyProtection` leaves it clean. The `sys_metadata` sentinel: `isCodeArtifactBody` answers false on it (code-artifact-provenance.ts 59), and the facade's package-less copy is stamped `_provenance: 'org'` under `RUNTIME_AUTHORED_PACKAGE_ID = 'sys_metadata'` (metadata-facade.ts 31, 193 to 196). Tenant rows: the only two `registerObject` calls in metadata-protocol are the save door's write-through (protocol.ts 17824) and the boot rehydration (29256), and both spread `_provenance: 'org'` onto the body before the call, so `isTenantAuthored` is true and the parse never runs; the `hydrateOverlayIntoRegistry` grafting path registers through `registerItem`, not `registerObject`. The tenant overlay row of a packaged action is therefore outside this door, which is what the card and the claim's ⛔ ask. **Right.** An `extend` body cannot carry `actions` at any authoring door (`ObjectExtensionSchema` guidance, object.zod.ts 4095) and the merge carries none, so the parse running on an extend contribution is inert.

**4. Stored shape equals the strict path's.** `ObjectSchema.actions` is `z.array(ActionSchema)` (object.zod.ts 3267) and nothing on `ObjectSchema` transforms an action after that element parse (every `objectName` reference in the file is a field diagnostic), so the registry now stores for a raw manifest exactly what `ObjectSchema.create` / strict `defineStack` store for the same declaration: `requiresFeature` / `requiresMembershipReach` removed and lowered into `visible` (grade gate first, feature gate last, action.zod.ts 2193 to 2198), defaults filled, CEL string wrapped. The new test pins the lowering against `ObjectSchema.create` on the same declaration and the registry's own `getObject` body against the served one; the control pins idempotence over already-parsed input (deep-equal). **Right.** The caller's body is not mutated by the parse (shallow copy, fresh `parsed.data`); the later in-place `applyProtection` stamp on that copy is pre-existing behaviour.

**5. Placement.** The parse sits after the field-`type` door and the two `extend` refusals and before `materializeTreeSelfReferences`, `applySystemFields`, `registerNamespace` and `openObjectEntry` (registry.ts 3489 to 3526), so a refused object leaves no contributor entry, no namespace claim and no short-name key; a refused re-registration never reaches the ownership block, so the sitting owner stays. The eighth test pins exactly that. **Right.**

**6. The two runtime fixture edits are fixes of off-contract fixtures, not loosening.** `stored-metadata-reader-contexts.pin.test.ts`: four `type: 'script'` actions on `pin_note` carried neither `body` nor `target`, which `ActionSchema` refuses (action.zod.ts 1970 to 1976). The edit adds `target` equal to the action name. Dispatch is `engine.executeAction` → `this.actions.get(objectName:actionName)` (engine.ts 6136), the handler `PIN_HANDLER_PLUGIN` registers by that key; `target` is never read for dispatch, only by `isHeadlessInvokableAction` as an executability bit (action-execution.ts 1008), and `AppPlugin` binds no handler for a target-bound script (plugin.ts 3699 / 3776), exactly as it bound none for a body-less one. The pins' assertions are untouched. `mcp-package-object-discovery.test.ts`: `ai: { exposed: true, description: 'Ping' }` violated `.min(40)` on `ai.description` (action.zod.ts 788); the edit supplies a 44-character description; the `listed` set and every assertion are unchanged. **Both right.**

**7. The producer measurement.** 21 objects / 154 actions / 0 changed / 4 refused, all four on `FLS_CONTRACT_OBJECT`: its `regrade`, `rename`, `invite`, `escalate` are `script` with no `body` or `target` (object-schema-fls-contract.ts 102 to 110). Its five in-repo readers (rest `meta-object-fls`, `meta-item-save-capability-gate`, `meta-compound-save-and-reset-capability-gate`, runtime `meta-object-fls`, metadata-core `object-schema-fls-references`) serve it from a stored map, a mocked `registry.getObject`, or `applyObjectSchemaMask` / `stageIssues`; none calls `registerObject` or `registerApp`. **Right**: this door never meets it today.

### ② Semver level

The changeset moves `@objectstack/objectql: patch` and nothing else; the runtime hunks are test files and `packages/spec/**` is untouched (the claim's ⛔ held). Under ruling A (check-changeset-no-major.mjs 905 to 925) the level is decided by the `Metadata-protocol:` line alone: `none` ⇒ every introduced entry `patch`; the `(narrowing)` arm keeps the BREAKING carriers and the ADR-0087 disposition and has no level coupling. The changeset carries all three carriers: the `!` on its summary, the `**BREAKING**` banner with Before / Now / Fix, and `Clause-②: no (narrowing: an object's own action that fails ActionSchema is refused at the runtime registration door, as #25649 did for standalone actions)`, byte-identical to the PR body's line. `Metadata-protocol: none` is true: `ActionSchema` and `ObjectSchema` are byte-unchanged and no authorable spelling moves. The ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is honest: the body has no `## Migration` / `迁移` header, no table whose header cells match `OLD_COLUMN_RE` / `NEW_COLUMN_RE` / `FROM` / `TO`; Before / Now / Fix bullets are a behaviour description, not a rewrite prescription. The PR title's `fix(objectql)!:` bang matches the banner. `Check Changeset` and `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` are `success` on the head. **The declared level matches what the diff publishes: patch, narrowing, breaking-flagged.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Card's open choice (refuse vs diagnostic).** The seat ruled refusal in claim 6409400948; the PR implements refusal, 422 `INVALID_METADATA`, and declares `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on body and changeset as the card and triage required. Answered.
- **Tenant overlay boundary (claim ⛔, card ⛔).** Kept; both protocol doors stamp `_provenance: 'org'` (① item 3). Answered.
- **`open_questions: []`.** None to answer.
- **Out-of-scope 1: `FLS_CONTRACT_OBJECT` off-contract.** Verified (① item 7). Its package CHANGELOG already records "not otherwise a spec-valid object (its `script` actions carry no `body` or `target`)" (metadata-core CHANGELOG.md 647). No door registers it under a package, so it has no reach today; a future suite that does will be refused with the `actions.N.body` issue, which is the contract working. Accepted as an acceptance note; no card owed.
- **Out-of-scope 2: doubled period.** Confirmed from `parsePackageAction` (`join('; ')` then `'. Every action…'`), pre-existing on `main` for standalone actions, no field of the envelope depends on it. Polish; accepted unfiled.
- **Deviation 1: no merge of `origin/main` before `pr_create`.** `main` since the base touched engine.ts (realtime refactor #25948) and a security fix (#25954), not registry.ts, action.zod.ts, code-artifact-provenance.ts or protection.zod.ts; the merge queue validates the merge. Accepted.
- **Deviation 2: ablation overlapped two ADR-0087 gate runs.** Those read changesets, not registry.ts, and the head's `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` re-answers them green. Accepted.
- **Reader note, not a flag the report raised.** At the nested-plugin door and the metadata-service reload doors the new refusal is swallowed into a `warn` by pre-existing catches (① item 2). Parity with every other registry refusal on those doors; named here so the next reader of "refused loudly" knows where it is a log line.
- **Pending CI.** Seven `Test Core` shards, `Build Core` and `Type Check · workspace` had not concluded at render time; they are gate verdicts of their own and this record does not stand in for them.
